hints.title: Find the turning points
hints.body: Differentiate the cubic, treating its constant parameter as fixed. Factor the derivative to locate the stationary inputs.
hints.recap: A vertical translation changes turning heights while leaving the stationary inputs fixed.
hints.pitfall: Two stationary points alone do not guarantee three axis crossings.
hints.pause: Find the stationary inputs and calculate their heights in the original cubic.

recall.reminder: A vertical translation changes turning heights while leaving the stationary inputs fixed.

hints.title: Place the extrema relative to the axis
hints.body: Use derivative signs to identify the local maximum and minimum. A positive-leading cubic has three distinct real roots exactly when its maximum is above the axis and its minimum is below it.
hints.recap: The three monotonic sections must each cross the axis.
hints.pitfall: Equality at a turning height gives a repeated root, so it does not produce three distinct roots.
hints.pause: Turn both height conditions into inequalities in the constant parameter, intersect them and check the boundaries.

recall.reminder: The three monotonic sections must each cross the axis.

solution:
1. Differentiate. With f(x)=2x3−3x2−12x+c, f′(x)=6(x−2)(x+1). Its signs are positive, negative, positive across −1 and 2.

2. Calculate the turning heights. The maximum is f(−1)=c+7 and the minimum is f(2)=c−20.

3. Require three distinct crossings. Both c+7>0 and c−20<0 must hold, so −7<c<20. At either boundary a turning point is on the axis and two roots coincide. Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Use cubic turning heights to obtain the strict parameter range for three distinct roots
